answer: A painted coastline fools no surveyor. Anyone can splash harbor blue on a chart, but depth is measured by dropping a weighted line until it rings against the floor. Honest work digs: it carves an inlet narrow enough to guard the water inside, and across epochs the cut deepens into canyon - cool, dark, pressure-tested. Sybil fleets run aground where the chart lied. Sound every claim; the echo tells you whether there is stone under the paint.
